text: Never judge Pay T M by its I P O. It crashed eighty six percent, then rose five point seven times. Multibagger, or trap?
November twenty twenty one. I P O price, two thousand one hundred fifty rupees. Day one close, one thousand five hundred sixty four. Down twenty seven percent.
January twenty twenty four. The R B I stopped Pay T M Payments Bank from taking deposits. By May, the stock hit three hundred ten rupees.
But here's the strange part. Today it's near one thousand seven hundred sixty nine. So what changed?
Latest results. Revenue up twenty eight percent. Profit, two hundred twenty five crore, versus twenty one crore a year ago.
Merchant payments, seven point one lakh crore, up twenty six percent. Financial services revenue, up forty nine percent.
But here's the catch. On November nineteen, it fell almost nine percent in a day, on a report that a new U P I fee may be delayed. And in April, the R B I cancelled the payments bank licence.

So, multibagger or trap? Both. It depends on when you bought. I P O buyers are still down eighteen percent. Buyers at the low have five point seven times. And the next leg needs a fee that isn't approved yet.
Save this, and send it to your friend who still holds Pay T M from the I P O. Education only, not investment advice. Follow money in cloud. Multibagger, or trap?
